title: Già la mensa è preparata
subtitle: Don Giovanni and Leporello: the opening of the finale from Don Giovanni, Act 2 (No. 24)

passages.label: Allegro vivace: Già la mensa è preparata · Voi suonate, amici cari · Giacchè spendo i miei danari
Leporello, presto in tavola! · Son prontissimo a servir · Giacchè spendo (again)
Allegretto (Una cosa rara): Bravi! · Che ti par del bel concerto? · Ah che piatto saporito!
Ah che barbaro appetito! · Nel veder i miei bocconi · Piatto! Servo!
Allegretto (Fra i due litiganti): Evvivano i litiganti · Versa il vino! · Questo pezzo di fagiano
Moderato (Non più andrai): Questo poi la conosco · Leporello! · Parla schietto · Non mi lascia una flussione
Mentre io mangio fischia un poco · Scusate! · Sì eccellente (to the bar before “L'ultima prova”)

licences.notes: Words as printed in the Schirmer vocal score: “Cosa rara!„ with the print's quotation marks, “vo'inghiottir” on one printed syllable, “Questo poi la conosco” (libretto Questa), “sò”, Leporello's “è'l” (libretto è il), Don Giovanni's “Cos' è?” on two notes, “Sì eccellente e il cuoco mio” (printed e without the accent, sung as è) and “anch' ei”. Both singers' last word, “provar”, is cut at the end of the piece: “pro-” here, “-var.” on the first bar of the next piece.

licences.source: G. Schirmer vocal score, New York 1900 (plate 15147, IMSLP #68957), pages 257–263, bars 1–199 of the Act 2 Finale (No. 24), from its beginning to the last bar of p. 263, before the Allegro assai “L'ultima prova dell'amor mio”
licences.author: G. Schirmer, piano reduction as printed
licences.notes: Written out from the printed pages in two chunks (pp. 257–260, bars 1–113; pp. 261–263, bars 114–199): the sung lines and the piano each read by two independent readers, every disagreement settled on the page by a judge, then checked bar by bar and checked again by fresh checkers, whose findings were corrected. The English singing translation and the stage directions are left out. Allegro vivace 4/4, D major, bars 1–46 (piano alone to bar 16); Allegretto 6/8, D major, bars 47–117 (the band plays from Martín y Soler's Una cosa rara); Allegretto 3/4, F major, bars 118–161 (Sarti's Fra i due litiganti); Moderato in cut time, B-flat major, bars 162–199 (“Non più andrai” from Figaro). One clear misprint was corrected: the piano's left hand in bars 178 and 180 is E natural. Single-chord tremolos are written as held chords. Fermatas in bars 72, 117 and 188 are held. Playback tempo: Allegro vivace ♩ = 180, Allegretto 6/8 ♩. = 80 (♩ = 120), Allegretto 3/4 ♩ = 170, Moderato ♩ = 123 (a half note ≈ 61), about 4:49 in all: the median of five complete recordings with this scene on its own track (Giulini 1959 4:36, Jacobs 2006 4:45, Iván Fischer 2026 4:49, Haitink 1984 4:50, C. Davis 1973 5:24), divided between the four sections as in Busch's 1936 Glyndebourne set, the only one found that gives each section its own track (1:02, 1:48, 0:47, 1:15). Mozart gives the words only.
